function.name: plan_tasks
function.description: Add new tasks to the shared todo list. Use small, concrete tasks that a single task loop can finish. When the goal produces a measurable output, register its expected shape in expectations before computing it.

expectations.description: Values the work is expected to produce, stated from the domain before any result exists: sign, units, order of magnitude, row count, output shape, latency bound. Immutable once registered; finish_task records observations against them and a mismatch is a defect in the model, not a caveat on the value.

expected.description: The expected value or range, with units or shape.

subject.description: What is being predicted (an output, a count, a measurement).

placement.description: Where to insert the new tasks: "next" places them immediately after the current task, before other pending work; "end" (default) appends them.

tasks.description: Tasks to append to the todo list, in execution order.

anyOf.description: A task title (worked in list order under the default role).

dependsOn.description: Ids of tasks (e.g. task-2) that must complete or drop before this task becomes workable. Use for work that genuinely cannot start earlier — not for ordinary ordering, which list position already expresses.

function.name: drop_task
function.description: Drop a task from the todo list when new information makes it unnecessary, redundant, or wrong. The task stays visible as dropped with your reason.

reason.description: Why this task is no longer needed.

function.name: revise_task
function.description: Rewrite a task's title when what you have learned changed what the task should actually do. Keeps its id, status, and notes.

function.name: finish_task
function.description: Finish the current task (or the task named by taskId). Use status completed with a summary of what was done, status blocked with a summary of why and what is needed, or status unreconciled when the work is complete and internally consistent but a pre-registered expectation does not match and you cannot reconcile it — list it under anomalies instead of explaining it away. Completing requires at least one passing correctness-class check (VERIFY with anchor.kind=external) or anchor="none" with an anchorNote saying why no external anchor exists.

anchor.description: How the completion is anchored. "external": a correctness-class check passed (the harness verifies this). "none": no external anchor exists for this claim; requires anchorNote and downgrades the completion in the run result.

anchorNote.description: Why no external anchor exists for this claim (required with anchor="none").

anomalies.description: With status unreconciled: each expectation the result could not be reconciled with.

note.description: What was tried and why the mismatch stands.

confidence.description: Your honest confidence that the finished work is correct, persisted on the task as a self-report.

observations.description: Observed values for pre-registered expectations. Every registered expectation must be observed before completion. A revised value for a subject already observed must cite evidence from outside the fix.

evidence.description: Evidence outside your own derivation that this value is closer to truth (required when the value changed from an earlier observation).

matches.description: Whether the observed value satisfies the expectation.

summary.description: What was done, or why the task is blocked and what would unblock it.

taskId.description: Optional task id. Defaults to the current task.

function.name: respond
function.description: Answer the goal directly and complete the run, when the goal is a question or asks for a status report and needs no workspace changes. The text is delivered to the user verbatim as the run's result. Not allowed while unfinished tasks exist.

text.description: The complete answer or report, in plain markdown.

function.name: observe
function.description: Save a short-lived observation for the next few task loops: a failing check's detail, an in-flight hypothesis, a result being verified. Observations expire after a few loops unless re-observed (which refreshes their ttl). Use remember instead for durable facts.

ttl.description: Optional number of task loops to keep the observation alive (default 4, capped).

function.name: recall
function.description: Recover the cached output of an earlier tool call this run (telemetry keeps an ends-kept copy of each call's last result) instead of re-running it. Match by tool name plus a fragment of the original input.

query.description: A fragment of the original call's input (a path, a command substring) to pick the right record.

toolName.description: The workspace tool whose earlier result you need (e.g. READ, BASH, GREP).

function.name: note_task
function.description: Append a progress note to a task (defaults to the current task) without ending the loop — partial findings, decisions, or where you left off. Use finish_task when the task is actually done or blocked.

taskId.description: Optional task id. Defaults to the current task.

function.name: remember
function.description:
Save a note to shared memory so future task loops can see it. Use for durable facts, decisions, and discovered constraints that matter for the rest of the run; for short-lived findings use observe.

Optional scope parameter:
- 'session' (default): saves to in-memory state for this run only.
- 'repo': persists the note into the project's memory bank stored under ~/.drip/projects/<project>/memory (outside the repo tree) so future sessions see it. Requires topic (a short title/slug for the page) and note. Optionally provide hook (one-line summary for the index). Use repo scope for durable, repo-specific knowledge: gotchas, key commands, architecture facts, persistent ideas.

scope.description: Where to save: 'session' (default, this run only) or 'repo' (persists to ~/.drip/projects/<project>/memory across sessions).

topic.description: Required for scope=repo. Short title for the memory page (e.g. 'Build Commands', 'Architecture'). Used as the page filename slug.

hook.description: Optional for scope=repo. One-line summary shown in the MEMORY.md index entry.

function.name: forget
function.description:
Remove a shared memory note by id when it is stale or wrong.

Optional scope parameter:
- 'session' (default): removes a note from in-memory state by noteId.
- 'repo': removes a topic page from the project's memory bank stored under ~/.drip/projects/<project>/memory (outside the repo tree) by slug. Use when repo-scoped knowledge is no longer accurate.

noteId.description: For scope=session: the memory note id to remove. For scope=repo: the slug of the topic page to remove (e.g. 'build-commands').

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the operator 1-4 staged multiple-choice clarification questions and block until they answer. Use ONLY when the goal is ambiguous or an approach tradeoff needs the operator's decision — preferably during planning, before implementing. Never ask anything the repository itself answers (read files and run tools first). Batch every question into this single call as one survey; put your best-guess option first in each list. After answers arrive, revise the plan with plan_tasks/revise_task before implementing.

questions.description: One to four questions, each with a short header, the question, and 2-4 options (best guess first).

allow_other.description: When true (the default) the operator may answer with free text instead of a listed option.

header.description: Short label shown above the question.

options.description: 2-4 choices; put your best guess first.

label.description: Short choice label recorded back as the answer's choice.
